scientific_question_matrix.question: Meaning of generative source
scientific_question_matrix.finding: Architecture-level equivalence is the evaluated target. Different trained instances sharing architecture, even different random seeds/datasets/schedules, are conceptually homologous. Instance-level identical parameters/training/configuration is separately defined, explicitly left for future work. No checkpoint/training-lineage or operator-identity evaluation demonstrated. Real images are grouped as one conceptual source regardless of camera.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Positive/negative pair construction
scientific_question_matrix.finding: For each target g: N real-real positives, N g-g positives, 2N other-g negatives; other may be real or another generator. Four N pairs per subset. Sampling/randomization/source-mixture weights not given.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Real-real/real-generated/generated-generated
scientific_question_matrix.finding: All three pair domains are specified. Real-real and same-source fake-fake are positive; real-fake and different-source fake-fake negative. Real images are not an individual-image authenticity prediction class.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Symmetry/equivalence
scientific_question_matrix.finding: Same-source labels form conceptual symmetric relation. Shared extractor plus cosine, absolute FFN difference or elementwise FFN product are symmetric mathematical comparators. No empirical swap test or transitive-consistency score; learned binary predictions need not form an equivalence relation. Common architecture/source grouping does not prove common operator.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Class balance
scientific_question_matrix.finding: N+N positives vs2N negatives: balanced4N per subset. Training N3500 yields14k/subset×16=224k total pairs; validation N500 implies2k/subset×16=32k; test N1000 yields4k/subset×17=68k. Unique image counts not stated.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Generator identity prediction vs pair construction
scientific_question_matrix.finding: Generator/source categories construct same/different labels; output is one homology score/binary pair label, not named source identity. NPR/POSE original tasks are adapted to pairwise embeddings.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Known/unseen GAN and diffusion protocols
scientific_question_matrix.finding: Train8GAN ForenSynths and8DM DiffusionForensics subsets; validate same datasets; test Self-Synthesis9GAN plus UniversalFakeDetect8 table groups (authors term8DM). Specific 16 training subset identities/checkpoints are not listed. DALL-E-mini appears in nominal DM group; do not silently treat it as a verified diffusion architecture.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Same-architecture vs same-instance comparison
scientific_question_matrix.finding: Architecture vs instance defined, but no controlled same-architecture/different-instance experiments or independent seeds/checkpoint enumeration; cannot show instance-level source separation or infer common training lineage.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Cross-family generalization
scientific_question_matrix.finding: Training mixture includes GAN and DM groups; OOD evaluates nominal9GAN+8DM. This is not train-only-GAN→heldout-DM or reverse. Cross-family-only transfer and exact architecture-disjointness are not established.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Semantic-content independence
scientific_question_matrix.finding: Intended to suppress semantics; cosine gap and asymmetric-augmentation interpretation motivate hypotheses. No explicit semantic holdout, content-matched same/different pairs, content-balanced generator setup or causal artifact intervention.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Positive/negative source/content overlap
scientific_question_matrix.finding: Pair labels described; no per-source pair matrix, content alignment, source-specific real-image controls, source-weighting counts or semantic-disjoint sampling. Common datasets/generator/content associations may supply shortcuts.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Train/test generator separation
scientific_question_matrix.finding: Authors call test generators unseen, using different named dataset collections. Exact 16 training entries and checkpoints are absent, with test LDM/ADM/Glide step configurations. Cannot independently certify architecture, version, seed and image-source disjointness. Validation uses same datasets, without explicit underlying image partition details.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Pair/shared-image leakage
scientific_question_matrix.finding: 224k/32k/68k are pairs, not independent unique images. No image-ID split manifests, dedup hashes, pair sampler seeds, disjoint original-image constraints or source-group bootstrap. Repeated image dependence and cross-split reuse not ruled out.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Model-instance leakage
scientific_question_matrix.finding: No instance/checkpoint inventory or seed/data lineage controls. Heldout subset terminology alone does not certify distinct model instances/architectures.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Embedding interaction strategies
scientific_question_matrix.finding: Cosine similarity uses cosine embedding loss with margin 0. Absolute shared-FFN subtraction or elementwise shared-FFN multiplication feed a one-layer classifier with BCE and sigmoid. Operation comparisons also change objective/head, so they do not isolate an interaction-only causal effect. Naive extractors use ResNet50.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Transfer detection/attribution representations
scientific_question_matrix.finding: NPR and POSE lose their original final classification layers; embeddings are integrated by elementwise multiplication. Compare frozen backbone with fine-tuning all parameters. Mean pair accuracy rises NPR 78.1→81.0 and POSE 74.1→76.6. Some subset bars worsen. Two models do not prove universal transfer behavior, and pair metrics are not separate authenticity or named-source scores.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Perturbation types/severities
scientific_question_matrix.finding: JPEG uses OpenCV/PIL and quality 75–100; Gaussian blur uses sigma Uniform[0,3.0]. Symmetric pairs receive the same perturbation type(s), including JPEG, blur, blur then JPEG, or neither. Asymmetric pairs receive different types. Mixed training randomly chooses symmetric/asymmetric; testing uses mixed perturbations. Exact probabilities, quality/sigma coupling, seeds and held-out severity schedule are unspecified.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Siamese architecture/training
scientific_question_matrix.finding: Shared fully convolutional extractor, global average pooling to a C-dimensional vector, naive ResNet50 backbone. Adam learning rate 5e-4, maximum 50 epochs, batch 32; five validation epochs without improvement trigger tenfold LR reduction, five more trigger stopping. Select best validation-accuracy checkpoint. Train resize 256², crop 224², horizontal flip probability 0.5; test original resolution. PyTorch 2.5.1, TorchVision 0.20.1, RTX 4090D. Exact FFN widths, pretraining/checkpoints, seeds and classification thresholds unspecified.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Metrics/confidence/baselines
scientific_question_matrix.finding: Pair accuracy and AP, homologous positive class. Printed means and derived rounded-cell means are retained separately with unresolved aggregation/rounding. No AUROC/EER, operating-point calibration, documented threshold-selection recipe, confidence intervals, repeated seeds or dependence correction. Baselines comprise generic interactions and adapted NPR/POSE, not separate authenticity or named-source protocols.

scientific_question_matrix.question: Negative findings/counterexamples
scientific_question_matrix.finding: Table2 LDM_100 cosine accuracy 68.3 exceeds multiplication 67.8. Table3 AttGAN mixed accuracy 76.0 exceeds asymmetric 74.8; symmetric AP 80.6 exceeds asymmetric 73.7. RelGAN symmetric AP 80.3 exceeds asymmetric 71.1. Other AP exceptions exist. Fine-tuning visibly worsens SNGAN, and NPR Glide_50_27. No exact values are invented for unlabeled figure bars. Average gains do not prove universal or causal benefits.

contribution_evaluation.rationale: The primary contribution is a formal architecture-level relational forensic task plus a research-question-driven characterization of its feasibility, representation transfer limitations and pair-specific robustness. The paper explicitly uses a generic minimal Siamese baseline rather than asserting a new specialized SOTA model. Section1 contributions2–3 and section4 preamble make evaluation/analysis a principal objective; three organized research questions compare operation families, two existing forensic representations and pair-augmentation regimes. Cross-representation transfer limitations and asymmetric/symmetric pair robustness remain informative about task behavior without retaining one proposed specific trained detector. These primary study questions go beyond tuning a named novel method. This decision is not based solely on first-systematic-study wording, table count, robustness plots or ablations.
contribution_evaluation.why_not_routine_method_validation_only: RQ1 interaction design and RQ3augmentation alone could be routine model tuning; independent support comes from the explicit task-science contribution structure, generic adopted framework and RQ2 transfer across detection/attribution models, with nonuniform findings. No new theory, causal proof or universally applicable design principle is inferred.
contribution_evaluation.contrary_interpretation: All empirical evidence uses a single Siamese framework, three extractors and limited public source collections; operation/head/loss changes and tuning confound interpretation. A maintainer could reasonably demand broader control before treating architecture-general scientific conclusions as established. This limits empirical confidence rather than erasing the explicitly primary systematic contribution.

bounded_precedents.R611: Accepted primary fingerprint-origin study varied architecture,seed,data and transformations. R024 is not equally strong on controlled source-instance origins; it studies relational task/representation/augmentation behavior. Do not infer its missing seed/instance analysis from R611.
bounded_precedents.R267: Accepted primary learned-quality/detectability investigation was informative before patch method; similarly R024 findings can be read as task-level study independently of a specific Siamese model. R267 does not automatically classify R024 and causality limitations remain separate.

contribution_evaluation.authoritative_remediation_if_accepted: Add analysis_study while retaining method. Preserve source_attribution and fully_generated. No change applied or authorized in this evidence-only wave.

negative_and_contradictory_evidence.finding: Multiplication leads mean accuracy/AP but not every cell: LDM_100 cosine accuracy 68.3 exceeds multiplication 67.8. Cosine versus multiplication also changes objective/head, so operation causality is not isolated.

Mean fine-tuning gains 2.9/2.5 percentage points do not mean every subset improves. SNGAN visibly worsens for both models; NPR Glide_50_27 also worsens. Individual bars are not numerically labeled, and no exact estimated score is claimed.

Asymmetry leads printed mean accuracy 74.7 and AP 76.9, but not every source/metric: AttGAN mixed accuracy 76.0>74.8, symmetric AP 80.6>asymmetric 73.7; RelGAN symmetric AP 80.3>asymmetric 71.1. Symmetric augmentation is not uniformly worse.

Authors call eight UniversalFakeDetect subsets DM-based, but DALL-E-mini appears in that group. Exact architecture taxonomy/provenance is not established here; nominal group counts are not independently verified model-family labels.

The paper motivates accountability and contrasts attribution with coarse family classification. Its actual experiments target architecture-level homology, not common operator, training lineage, exact checkpoint or same-instance verification. The narrative is not a restriction on all prior attribution literature.

Semantic independence, intrinsic traces, web deployment utility and causal augmentation explanations are interpretations, without explicit content holdouts, artifact interventions or real deployment experiments.

Use reconciled display-cell transcription and derived means in this packet. Original frozen worker transcription contains separately documented cell errors. Printed AP summaries remain unchanged; aggregation and rounding uncertainty remain.

method_questions.question: Stable Diffusion backbone and version
method_questions.finding: Figure 1 explicitly labels SD v1.5 inversion and denoising. Section 3 describes a fixed pretrained Stable Diffusion latent model, mapping 512×512×3 RGB images to 64×64×4 latents. The exact feature-extractor weight revision is not specified in the main paper.
method_questions.locator: PDF p.1 Fig.1 and p.4 §3; printed pp.10759,10762

method_questions.question: Inversion procedure
method_questions.finding: Text-conditioned DDIM inversion Fθ is followed by reverse sampling Rθ (Equations 1–4). The authors omit classifier-free guidance and per-image null-text fine-tuning. The exact step count and scheduler configuration are not specified in the authorized main manuscript.

method_questions.question: Inversion inputs/intermediate representations
method_questions.finding: VAE encoding maps x to z0; conditional forward inversion produces the approximate noise map ẑT; reverse sampling produces reconstructed latent ẑ0. The VAE decoder maps both noise and reconstruction to image space.

method_questions.question: Reconstruction and residual features
method_questions.finding: The detector concatenates the original image x, decoded noise D(ẑT), and decoded reconstruction D(ẑ0). The absolute reconstruction residual |x−D(ẑ0)| is a separate ablation and DIRE comparison, not the full method’s input representation.

method_questions.question: Prompts and text conditioning
method_questions.finding: An automatic BLIP-2 caption, called BLIP in later text, is encoded with CLIP to condition both inversion and reconstruction. The original image-generation prompt is not required. Exact captioner and text-encoder weight revisions are not verified.

method_questions.question: Training generator identities
method_questions.finding: Two separate training regimes are reported: 350k class-conditioned ProGAN fake images with LSUN reals; or 300k Stable Diffusion v1 fake images from DiffusionDB with 300k random LAION reals. The SD v1 training-image family should not be confused with the SD v1.5 feature extractor.

method_questions.question: Training real image sources
method_questions.finding: LSUN supplies the real population in the ProGAN regime, and 300k random LAION images supply it in the SD regime. The main manuscript does not provide the exact LSUN real count or membership lists. Dataset-source overlap was not independently checked.

method_questions.question: Classifier architecture
method_questions.finding: The classifier is a ResNet50 trained from scratch with binary cross-entropy and a scalar real/fake prediction logit. The best checkpoint is selected on a held-out set from the same source as training. Augmentations precede inversion: flip, crop, color jitter, grayscale, cutout, noise, blur, JPEG and rotate. No generator-identity output is trained or evaluated.

method_questions.question: Inference-time computation
method_questions.finding: Inference requires image captioning, text encoding, VAE encoding, iterative SD U-Net forward DDIM inversion and reverse DDIM reconstruction, two VAE decodes, and ResNet50 classification. There is no per-image fine-tuning or classifier-free guidance. The main manuscript supplies no exact latency, step count, memory, hardware or FLOP measurement; only qualitative extra cost over an RGB-only pass is supported.

method_questions.question: DIRE/resynthesis distinction
method_questions.finding: The complete representation includes decoded noise and conditioned reconstruction as well as RGB, unlike an RGB-only detector or an absolute-DDIM-residual detector. The paper warns that the official DIRE checkpoint has an issue discussed in an unavailable appendix, so the 0.493 average does not settle the ideal DIRE algorithm’s performance. Table 4 also reports ProGAN-trained DALL-E 3 residual AUROC 0.672 above the complete model’s 0.642. The Equation 8 likelihood argument depends on a first-order approximation and model-misspecification assumptions; it does not verify a calibrated likelihood estimator.
method_questions.locator: PDF pp.4–5 §3–4; p.7 Table 3; p.8 Table 4

benchmark_questions.question: SynRIS name and definition
benchmark_questions.finding: The paper names the protocol SynRIS and expands RIS as reverse image search. It does not explicitly spell out a full expansion of the SynRIS name. The protocol constructs a corresponding real-image evaluation population for each synthetic-generator population and evaluates binary authenticity discrimination.

benchmark_questions.question: Acquisition procedure
benchmark_questions.finding: A reverse-image-search API is queried with each fake image to find a visually and thematically similar real image. Matches must occur on pages created before 2021-01-01. The main manuscript does not identify the API vendor, query settings, candidate rank, matching score or acceptance threshold.

benchmark_questions.question: Synthetic generators
benchmark_questions.finding: Table 3 evaluates 15 new populations: DALL-E 2, DALL-E 3, Midjourney v5/6 and Imagen, plus Kandinsky 2, Kandinsky 3, PixArt-α, Playground 2.5, SDXL-DPO, SDXL, Seg-MOE, SSD-1B, Stable-Cascade, Segmind Vega and Würstchen 2. Table 1 says eleven open-source populations, but its footnote lists only ten and omits Playground 2.5, which appears in Table 3 and the project page. Exact checkpoint revisions are not recoverable from this main manuscript.

benchmark_questions.question: Real matching criteria
benchmark_questions.finding: Each selected Internet real is intended to be visually and thematically similar to its fake query and to occur on a pre-2021 page. “Real” means not generated by a text-to-image model, even when another tool such as Photoshop was used. This definition does not establish an unmanipulated-photograph ground truth or perfect semantic/style balance.

benchmark_questions.question: One-to-one versus set-level
benchmark_questions.finding: The procedure describes a corresponding real image for each fake, and Table 1 reports equal real/fake sizes. Scoring is aggregate binary AUROC, not a pairwise similarity metric. The main text does not establish globally unique real matches, a bijection, or deduplication within and across generator populations.

benchmark_questions.question: Original versus selected sources
benchmark_questions.finding: DALL-E 2 fakes come from Corvi et al.; DALL-E 3 from laion/dalle-3-dataset; Midjourney from wanng/midjourney-v5-202304-clean; Imagen from the authors’ API generations; and open-source fakes from author generations conditioned on Midjourney prompts. Real evaluation images are selected through Internet reverse search. Training remains ProGAN+LSUN or SD+LAION, not a claimed SynRIS training population.

benchmark_questions.question: Matching modality
benchmark_questions.finding: Matching is described as visual, thematic and stylistic, using image queries. It is not an explicitly specified textual-nearest-neighbor algorithm or a semantic oracle. The main manuscript gives no exact matching embedding, score, rank threshold or independent human matching-quality audit.

benchmark_questions.question: Matching-score distributions
benchmark_questions.finding: No per-pair search-score histogram or distribution is supplied. Table 2’s FID and KID are aggregate real/fake distribution distances, not distributions of reverse-search matching scores. For Imagen, LAION gives FID 127.1 / printed KID 2.1, WebLI 101.9 / 1.2, and RIS 83.6 / 0.2. KID is printed on a ×10⁻² scale.

benchmark_questions.question: Sample size
benchmark_questions.finding: Table 1 prints balanced pairs: DALL-E 2 700/700, DALL-E 3 3.3k/3.3k, Midjourney 4.4k/4.4k, Imagen 700/700, and eleven open-source populations each 3.5k/3.5k. The “k” counts are rounded printed values, not verified exact downloadable membership. The ordering of the two classes in the imbalanced academic DALL-E 2 1k/5k row is not independently established here.

benchmark_questions.question: Train/validation/test restrictions
benchmark_questions.finding: Training uses ProGAN+LSUN or SD+LAION, with checkpoint selection on held-out data from the same training source. SynRIS populations are test/evaluation populations from other named generator sources. Exact split IDs and resampling counts are absent from the main paper. Shared SD lineage among some test models prevents equating unseen named generators with a complete architecture-family holdout.
benchmark_questions.locator: PDF p.3 Fig.2; pp.5–6 §4; p.7 Table 3

benchmark_questions.question: Duplicate and source leakage
benchmark_questions.finding: The pre-2021 page cutoff aims to reduce contamination of the real class by modern text-to-image generations. It does not constitute cross-split perceptual deduplication, source-host blocking, or prompt-family blocking. LAION and generator pretraining data could overlap Internet reals found by search. Actual overlap is unknown because membership and image assets were not inspected.

benchmark_questions.question: Search ranking selection bias
benchmark_questions.finding: The main manuscript does not audit search ranking, language/geographic coverage, source domains, failed-query rates or index bias. Similarity search selects publicly indexed, discoverable images and may introduce topic, style or provenance selection effects. These are reviewer-identified possible confounds, not measured paper findings.

benchmark_questions.question: Temporal authenticity safeguard
benchmark_questions.finding: The stated rule retains matches on pages created before 2021-01-01, preceding the original DALL-E announcement and the evaluated diffusion releases. Page creation dates are not forensic verification of each image’s original creation or upload date and do not rule out later asset replacement or all older forms of generated imagery.

benchmark_questions.question: Temporal stability and reproducibility
benchmark_questions.finding: The main paper does not document search date, vendor, index version or ranking logs. Announced JSON real-image URLs and fake prompts/seeds could make a fixed release more reusable but do not eliminate URL decay, changed API models or unavailable checkpoints. The announced archive was not inspected.

benchmark_questions.question: Real/fake class balance
benchmark_questions.finding: SynRIS’s printed counts are balanced per generator. The academic DALL-E 2 row is imbalanced at 1k/5k, while Craiyon and LDM each use 1k/1k. The main metric is AUROC; AP, accuracy and additional curves are referred to appendices that were not retrieved. Equal class counts do not establish equal semantic distributions or deployment class prevalence.

benchmark_questions.question: Baseline populations and scoring
benchmark_questions.finding: Table 3 applies a common AUROC comparison to DIRE, CNNDet, DMDet, UFD and FakeInversion on the listed evaluation populations. Table 2 changes the real population while retaining the same fakes and fixed 0.8 recall threshold for UFD. Images are resized to 256 px on the shortest side and saved losslessly. Shared populations are described, not independently byte-verified. DMDet’s right-panel LDM training and the DIRE checkpoint issue remain explicit limitations.

benchmark_questions.question: Relative ranking sensitivity
benchmark_questions.finding: Ranks differ across evaluation populations. Under SD-family training, academic DALL-E 2 has DMDet 0.727 > UFD 0.590 > Ours 0.571, while SynRIS DALL-E 2 has UFD 0.776 > Ours 0.747 > DMDet 0.672. For SDXL, CNNDet 0.814 > Ours 0.807. Under ProGAN training, academic Craiyon gives UFD 0.974 > Ours 0.874, while SynRIS DALL-E 3 gives Ours 0.642 > UFD 0.323. Different fake populations may also differ, so these are not pure causal effects of real-image matching. Table 2’s fixed-fake experiment establishes UFD sensitivity to the chosen real population, not a controlled ranking shift across every detector.

benchmark_questions.question: In-the-wild validity claim
benchmark_questions.finding: The paper claims alignment with in-the-wild detector performance. The concrete main-paper support is a comparison to Imagen’s WebLI real-image training population and increased UFD/FID/KID difficulty under RIS. There is no independently sampled deployment benchmark, numerical cross-detector correlation coefficient, confidence interval or causal validation in the authorized main manuscript. WebLI FPR 0.559/0.664 differs from RIS 0.620/0.720; their FID/KID also differ. “Closely aligns” must not be restated as equality or proven universal real-world validity.
benchmark_questions.locator: PDF p.1 abstract; p.6 Table 2; p.7 §5

benchmark_questions.question: Release and evaluation implementation
benchmark_questions.finding: The project announces code, JSON real-image URLs and fake prompts/seeds in one Google-hosted ZIP, and provides thirteen preview links excluding DALL-E 2 and Imagen. The ZIP was not saved, extracted or read. A preinterruption web-viewer probe reported unsupported ZIP MIME; its transferred HTTP payload is unknown. One exact project-website GitHub metadata request returned 403 rate-limit, so no commit was pinned and no executable scoring interface, split membership or archive license was verified.

benchmark_questions.question: Reuse by independent future detectors
benchmark_questions.finding: Introduction contributions 3–5, Section 6’s invitation, per-generator population construction, common metrics, independent baseline comparisons and the separate release announcement establish an evaluation protocol intended for independent detectors. Applying binary AUROC does not require the FakeInversion feature extractor. This is strong evidence for an independent R2 contribution, while actual operation of the announced release remains unverified.
benchmark_questions.locator: PDF p.2 contributions; p.6 Tables 1–2; p.7 Table 3; p.8 §6

primary_contribution_evidence: Introduction contributions 3–5 separately propose, verify and release the evaluation protocol after method contributions 1–2.
Section 4/Table 1 defines fifteen new per-generator populations, reverse-search acquisition, the pre-2021 cutoff, preprocessing and binary AUROC scoring.
Table 2 changes the real population with fixed fakes and recall for an existing independent UFD detector, demonstrating evaluation sensitivity beyond validating FakeInversion.
Table 3 compares four external detector families and the proposed method on new and prior benchmarks, with the original training/checkpoint qualifications retained.
Section 6 explicitly invites future independent detector research using the new resources; the project announces a URLs/prompts/seeds/code package, whose contents remain unverified.
contrary_or_limiting_evidence: The paper’s unconditional bias-free/“ensure” language is stronger than the demonstrated matching and FID/KID evidence.
No search score/rank threshold, API vendor, search timestamp, uniqueness/deduplication or source-host controls are specified; perfect semantic matching is not established.
Table 3 SD-trained DALL-E 2: UFD 0.776 exceeds Ours 0.747; SDXL: CNNDet 0.814 exceeds Ours 0.807. Other detectors win the three academic rows in one or both training panels.

Table 4 ProGAN-trained DALL-E 3: residual 0.672 exceeds Ours 0.642. Many open-source Ours cells differ from Table 3 without main-text reconciliation; SDXL is 0.764/0.807 in Table 3 and 0.691/0.884 in Table 4.
Table 2 WebLI and RIS metrics are not identical. The main paper contains no independently measured numerical deployment-correlation coefficient.
Pairwise acquisition does not establish causal validity, representative deployment prevalence, or generalization across all generator families.
DIRE’s official checkpoint has a reported issue; right-panel DMDet uses an LDM checkpoint rather than the same SD training source.
Table 1’s footnote lists ten open models despite the stated eleven; Playground 2.5 appears in Table 3 and the author project.
Code, URLs, prompts and seeds are announced; archive contents, scoring interfaces, splits and licenses were not inspected. The website repository pin attempt failed with 403 rate-limit.
scientific_review.judgment_reason: Locked R2 includes a reusable evaluation protocol or systematic comparative framework. SynRIS explicitly contributes method-independent evaluation-population construction and scoring, compares independent detectors and controlled real populations, and invites future reuse. The judgment does not follow merely from large tables or many generators. Unverified release contents lower operational-reproduction confidence without erasing the demonstrated scientific evaluation-protocol contribution.
scientific_review.empirical_validity_confidence: medium; conclusions are bounded to the evaluated populations and matching proxies
scientific_review.operational_reproducibility_confidence: low; archive contents, executable interfaces, assets, splits and reproduced metrics remain unverified
limitations: Exact DDIM steps, hyperparameters, latency and configurations are delegated to appendices not retrieved under this evidence budget.
No exact membership/split lists, asset checksums, near-duplicate audit, training-data overlap or licensing rights were verified.
No arXiv body or IEEE-final bytes were retrieved. The CVF accepted-version equivalence statement is preserved without claiming exhaustive version equality.
The release announcement does not establish executable interfaces, exact split files or current stability of real-image URLs.
The R2 judgment does not reopen existing method/dataset roles, add an analysis role or change any task.

R1.final_rule: Assign dataset only when construction, release, curation, or systematic provision of a reusable dataset/data resource is itself a substantive paper contribution. Data generated or collected solely to run the paper's experiments is insufficient.

R2.final_rule: Assign benchmark only when the paper contributes a reusable evaluation benchmark, challenge, protocol, systematic comparative framework, or benchmark resource intended to evaluate methods. Large experimental tables or evaluation across many generators alone are insufficient.

R3.final_rule: Assign analysis_study only when systematic empirical or theoretical analysis is a primary scientific contribution. Routine ablations, robustness tables, parameter sweeps, or supporting interpretability figures do not qualify by themselves.

curated:1a8e996ef9ce73efc0ef.title: AI-Generated Image Homology Detection
curated:1a8e996ef9ce73efc0ef.authors: Hang Gao; Rui Ba; Kaiye Yu; Han Xing; Mengting Hu
curated:1a8e996ef9ce73efc0ef.venue: International Conference on Knowledge Science, Engineering and Management
curated:1a8e996ef9ce73efc0ef.venue_name: International Conference on Knowledge Science, Engineering and Management
curated:1a8e996ef9ce73efc0ef.raw_venue: International Conference on Knowledge Science, Engineering and Management
curated:1a8e996ef9ce73efc0ef.abstract: The rapid proliferation of AI-generated images has raised growing concerns about content authenticity and accountability. Existing image forensic studies mainly focus on detection and attribution, aiming to determine whether an image is generated or to identify its source model. However, these approaches rely on stable and generalizable class-level evidence, and often become unreliable when generative models evolve or visual artifacts diminish. In this work, we introduce AI-generated image homology detection, a new forensic task that asks a fundamentally different question: whether two images originate from the same generative source, regardless of whether that source can be explicitly identified. Unlike detection and attribution, homology detection formulates image forensics as a relational problem rather than a categorical one, enabling forensic analysis even when absolute judgments are uncertain or unavailable. We present the first systematic study of this task. Using a generic Siamese framework, we demonstrate that homology detection is feasible across diverse generative models, including unseen GANs and diffusion models. Through extensive experiments, we analyze embedding interaction strategies, examine the transferability of detection and attribution models, and investigate robustness under realistic image perturbations. Our results reveal that naive homology detectors already establish meaningful baselines, while transferred detection and attribution models exhibit limited generalization. Moreover, we show that asymmetric data augmentation plays a critical role in improving robustness for pairwise forensic analysis. Overall, this work positions homology detection as an orthogonal and complementary capability to existing forensic tasks, and provides new insights into relational modeling for AI-generated image forensics in open and evolving web environments. Our code is available at https://github.com/gaohangcodes/AI-generated-Image-Homology-Detection.

curated:1eef07ebb6bd7e596f61.title: FakeInversion: Learning to Detect Images from Unseen Text-to-Image Models by Inverting Stable Diffusion
curated:1eef07ebb6bd7e596f61.authors: George Cazenavette, Avneesh Sud, Thomas Leung, Ben Usman
curated:1eef07ebb6bd7e596f61.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
curated:1eef07ebb6bd7e596f61.venue_name: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
curated:1eef07ebb6bd7e596f61.raw_venue: 2024 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
curated:1eef07ebb6bd7e596f61.abstract: Due to the high potential for abuse of GenAl systems, the task of detecting synthetic images has recently become of great interest to the research community. Unfortunately, ex-isting image-space detectors quickly become obsolete as new high-fidelity text-to-image models are developed at blinding speed. In this work, we propose a new synthetic image detector that uses features obtained by inverting an open-source pre-trained Stable Diffusion model. We show that these inversion features enable our detector to generalize well to unseen generators of high visual fidelity (e.g., DALL.E 3) even when the detector is trained only on lower fidelity fake images generated via Stable Diffusion. This detector achieves new state-of-the-art across multiple training and evaluation se-tups. Moreover, we introduce a new challenging evaluation protocol that uses reverse image search to mitigate stylistic and thematic biases in the detector evaluation. We show that the resulting evaluation scores align well with detectors' in-the-wild performance, and release these datasets as public benchmarks for future research.

Contributions 3-5, section 4 and Tables 1-3 define SynRIS evaluation separately from RGB plus SDv1.5 inversion-derived detector features. SD-trained DALL-E 2 UFD 0.776 exceeds FakeInversion 0.747; SDXL CNNDet 0.814 exceeds 0.807.
